title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 establishes comprehensive regulations for AI development and deployment in the United States, aiming to ensure transparency, accountability, and public safety. It outlines standards for data use, algorithmic fairness, and oversight mechanisms to prevent misuse and promote responsible AI innovation.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: Congress supports the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, saying it safeguards consumers and keeps electricity affordable. It also aims to make sure all Americans—homes, small businesses, schools, hospitals and farms—continue to receive reliable, affordable energy even as AI and data‑center growth expands.

title: Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025
action: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Energy. Hearings held. With printed Hearing: S.Hrg. 119-366.
summary: The Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 proposes regulations to encourage the use of liquid cooling technologies in AI systems, aiming to improve energy efficiency and reduce heat generation. It also sets guidelines for manufacturers and operators to ensure safety, compliance, and environmental standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to address the environmental footprint of AI technologies, such as energy consumption and electronic waste. It sets standards and regulations to ensure that the development and deployment of AI are carried out in a more environmentally responsible manner.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to regulate how artificial intelligence systems collect, store, and use data. It seeks to protect individual privacy, promote transparency in AI data practices, and set clear standards for accountability and data security.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies to evaluate and mitigate bias, errors, and potential harms in AI systems, ensuring that algorithms do not produce discriminatory or unsafe outcomes. It establishes regulatory oversight and transparency standards, giving regulators the power to enforce accountability and protect consumers from unfair or harmful algorithmic decisions.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is a proposed law that aims to protect the personal data of children and teenagers from being collected, stored, or used by AI systems without proper safeguards. It sets strict rules for consent, transparency, and accountability to ensure young people’s privacy rights are respected in the development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes safety standards for AI-enabled toys sold to children, ensuring they meet rigorous testing for privacy, data security, and physical safety. It also sets mandatory disclosure requirements for manufacturers regarding how these toys collect, store, and use data about young users.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act aims to broaden the range of voices and perspectives represented in AI-generated content, encouraging developers to include more diverse linguistic, cultural, and demographic inputs. By promoting inclusivity and reducing bias, the act seeks to make AI systems more reflective of the real world and better serve all users.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act aims to regulate the use and integration of AI technologies in physical systems such as robots, drones, and autonomous vehicles. It establishes guidelines, safety standards, and oversight mechanisms to ensure responsible deployment and coordination among developers, operators, and regulators.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act would put a hold on the creation and expansion of new artificial intelligence data centers, ensuring that any new projects go through a thorough environmental and regulatory review. The moratorium also calls for an assessment of current data centers to confirm they meet updated standards for energy use, emissions, and community impact.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2026 is a federal law designed to broaden access to artificial‑intelligence learning in schools and universities. It allocates resources for curriculum development, teacher training, and educational research so that AI concepts are integrated into classrooms nationwide.

title: CREATE AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The CREATE AI Act is a proposed set of laws aimed at governing the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence to ensure transparency, fairness, and accountability. It seeks to protect users, promote responsible innovation, and set standards for safety and privacy in AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act proposes a framework for collecting, managing, and sharing data in a way that makes it easier to develop and use AI technologies. It aims to standardize data practices, improve data quality, protect privacy, and promote fairness while encouraging innovation.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act sets out legal guidelines for the use of AI in vocational education and training. It seeks to ensure that AI tools used in training environments are safe, transparent, and supportive of learners while encouraging responsible innovation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 is a law that requires developers and companies to assess and report the potential risks of their AI systems before they are released to the public. It sets up a framework for ongoing monitoring and oversight to protect consumers, businesses, and national security from harmful or unintended AI behavior.

title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026
action: Star Print ordered on the bill.
summary: The Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026 is designed to encourage responsible AI development while safeguarding public interests. It proposes new regulations, funding for research, and oversight mechanisms to ensure AI technologies are used safely, ethically, and in ways that benefit society.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 seeks to give small businesses the knowledge and skills needed to use AI effectively. It sets up a federal program that offers free or low‑cost AI training, resources, and support to help small business owners and employees stay competitive in a rapidly evolving digital economy.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act seeks to help small businesses adopt and integrate AI technologies by providing funding, training, and resources. It also establishes guidelines and incentives to encourage innovation while protecting consumer privacy and promoting economic growth in the small‑business sector.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act aims to streamline and modernize AI regulation by removing or easing existing barriers for developers and users. It seeks to promote innovation while ensuring safety and accountability through updated legal frameworks.

title: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act aims to protect consumers from fraud and deceptive practices that use artificial intelligence. It establishes rules for companies that develop or deploy AI technologies, requiring transparency, safeguards, and penalties to stop AI‑generated scams.

title: States' Right to Regulate AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The States' Right to Regulate AI Act affirms that individual U.S. states have the authority to enact and enforce their own regulations on artificial intelligence. It sets a framework that allows states to tailor AI policies to local priorities while ensuring that federal guidelines remain in place.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 would set out legal standards to ensure that AI systems do not violate civil rights, such as by avoiding biased or discriminatory outcomes. It would also establish oversight and accountability mechanisms so that developers, users, and regulators can enforce these standards and address any civil rights violations that arise.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act proposes a framework for developing and supporting a skilled workforce in artificial intelligence and other critical technologies. It aims to create training, educational programs, and talent pipelines that help the nation remain competitive and secure in these high‑impact fields.

title: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025 is designed to safeguard U.S. national security by blocking foreign adversaries from creating or deploying AI technologies that could harm U.S. interests. It sets up oversight and enforcement mechanisms to ensure AI systems remain secure and free from hostile foreign influence.

title: TEST AI Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The TEST AI Act of 2025 is a proposed set of regulations aimed at governing the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems. It seeks to establish standards for safety, transparency, and accountability in AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The act establishes a federal program to boost public understanding and literacy about artificial intelligence. It calls for the creation of educational resources, outreach initiatives, and funding to support AI awareness and learning nationwide.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 establishes rules for how the Small Business Administration will use and manage artificial intelligence technologies in its operations and services. It requires clear policies on transparency, privacy, and ethical use, along with oversight mechanisms to ensure compliance and protect small businesses and the public from potential AI risks.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a law designed to regulate and supervise artificial intelligence systems that can modify their own code or behavior. It requires developers to implement monitoring safeguards, report updates, and ensure that self‑improving AI remains safe, transparent, and under human oversight.

title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act proposes a framework to evaluate how generative AI might be used to plan or facilitate terrorism, ensuring such technologies are monitored and regulated. It aims to prevent misuse while allowing legitimate innovation in AI development.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act aims to evaluate and reduce the environmental impacts that artificial intelligence systems can have, such as energy consumption and carbon emissions. It sets guidelines and reporting requirements for companies to ensure AI development and deployment are more sustainable and environmentally responsible.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 ensures that medical care decisions remain in the hands of qualified human doctors, limiting the role of artificial intelligence in diagnosing and treating patients. It requires that any AI tools used in healthcare be supplementary, with oversight and final responsibility resting with licensed physicians.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: This act aims to boost the export of AI technologies across the entire technology stack—hardware, software, and services—by providing incentives and easing regulatory hurdles. It also seeks to position the country as a global leader in AI supply chains, promoting economic growth while upholding international compliance standards.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act aims to position the United States as a global leader in open‑source artificial intelligence by encouraging the development and sharing of AI tools, models, and research. It calls for increased government investment, incentives for industry collaboration, and policies that promote transparency, interoperability, and public benefit in AI technologies.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 establishes standards and safeguards for using AI in veteran services, aiming to protect beneficiaries from bias, privacy violations, and unsafe outcomes. It also creates oversight mechanisms to ensure that AI tools deployed in the VA system are transparent, accountable, and aligned with veterans’ best interests.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to strengthen the protection of AI systems by setting standards and protocols for their security. It requires organizations to evaluate risks, implement safeguards, and report on compliance to ensure AI technology remains safe and trustworthy.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 is a proposed law aimed at reducing unfairness in AI and algorithmic decision‑making by setting strict transparency and testing requirements for developers. It would establish oversight mechanisms and penalties to ensure that algorithms used in public and private sectors are regularly audited for bias and corrected before they can harm individuals or groups.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is designed to safeguard U.S. AI models from unauthorized copying and exploitation by establishing stronger legal penalties for theft and misuse. It requires companies to adopt robust security practices, disclose breaches, and comply with new licensing standards to protect intellectual property in AI.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 aims to hold companies that use AI systems responsible for the impacts of their algorithms. It requires firms to evaluate, document, and mitigate bias, risk, and safety concerns in automated decision‑making processes.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act establishes requirements for defense agencies to rigorously test, validate, and certify AI systems before they are deployed in military operations, ensuring these systems meet high standards of safety, accuracy, and reliability. It also mandates a formal reporting process for any incidents, failures, or unexpected behavior involving defense AI, thereby promoting transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement of AI technologies in the national security domain.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires the government to compile and publish a comprehensive annual report on the development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies in China, assessing their technical capabilities, economic impact, and societal implications. The act aims to provide transparency, guide policy decisions, and ensure that AI growth aligns with national strategic priorities and ethical standards.
